fields.h1: Build a Parent Survey for Your School or PTO
fields.hero_description: Build a parent survey families can answer in English or Spanish, with results by school or grade in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a School Needs From a Parent Survey
fields.features_subheading: Families answer in the language they read best, and each result reaches the staff member who can act on it.
fields.feature_1:
English and Spanish from one survey

Let each family pick a language on the first screen. Both versions write to the same table. A Spanish answer and an English answer to question 4 land in one column and one chart.
fields.feature_2:
No names, and small groups held back

Leave name and email off the survey and say so before the first question. Set a minimum, such as 5 answers, and any grade or classroom below it stays out of the results view.
fields.feature_3:
Results by school, grade, or program

Ask for the child's grade or school in question 1, and every chart can split on it. A principal sees one building, and the district office sees every school next to its goal.
fields.feature_4:
Sent when the meeting or term ends

Send the survey after an event the school tracks, like an annual IEP meeting or the last week of a term. Each family gets one link per child, and a reminder follows a week later.
fields.feature_5:
A low result reaches the right person

Post to a Slack channel or email one staff member when a result crosses a line you set. A school under its goal or a grade over its homework guideline reaches the person who owns it.
fields.feature_6:
Your answers, your database, your code

Keep every answer as a row in a database you own, with no cap on responses. On paid plans, export the full survey app to your GitHub repository and change it as the school needs.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Parent Surveys and Who Reads Them
fields.tab_content_1:
Pine Hollow falls below 65%

Harlow Creek School District surveys each family after its child's annual IEP meeting. By May, 418 families had answered, and 298 agreed the school helped them take part in planning. At Pine Hollow Elementary, only 29 of 50 agreed, below the goal of at least 65%. Director Dana Whitfield set up a family meeting there.
fields.tab_content_2:
Grade 8 homework runs 74 minutes a night

Bellmont Middle School asked parents how many minutes of homework their child does on a school night. In one week, 286 parents answered. Grades 6 and 7 averaged 41 and 52 minutes. Grade 8 reached 74, over the school's 60-minute guideline, and the grade 8 team moved its weekly project into class time.
fields.tab_content_3:
27 of 64 replies came in Spanish

Little Fern Early Learning Center closes each school year with a family survey in English and Spanish, and families pick a language before the first question. This June, 64 of its 78 families answered, and 27 chose Spanish. A later pickup time led the requests with 31 families, and the list went to director Lucia Ferraro.
fields.tab_content_4:
Shade sails win the vote with 109

The Juniper Road PTO had spring fundraiser money and three projects to choose from: shade sails over the playground, new library books, or a music cart. In 10 days, 233 families voted. Shade sails won with 109 votes to 74 for library books and 50 for the music cart. The tally posted to the PTO board's Slack channel.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Parent Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write a parent survey families will answer in their own language, then share back what it changed.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the decision the answers will feed before you write a question: a homework guideline, a pickup time, or what the PTO funds. If no decision is waiting on the results, families give up their time and see nothing change.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about what a parent sees firsthand: homework at the kitchen table, the messages that come home, and how staff treat their child. Leave classroom teaching to a student survey, since parents only hear about lessons through their child.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Aim for about 10 questions a parent can answer on a phone while waiting at pickup. Time it with two parents before launch, and drop any question whose answer would not change what the school does next.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Check enrollment records for the languages families speak at home, and have a fluent staff member read every translated version before it goes out. Keep the question order identical in each language, and compare results line by line.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell parents on the first screen who will read their answers and whether names are kept. If staff need to follow up with anyone, ask for contact details in an optional last question and keep everything before it anonymous.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Post the link in the school app, print a QR code on the take-home folder, and set out a laptop at conferences. Families who never open school email still pass the front office or wait in the pickup line.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Within a month, send families a short summary with how many answered, the findings that matter, and what the school will change. Open next year's survey by naming one change that came from this one.

faq_plan.a: A parent survey is a short set of questions a school or district sends to families to learn how a child's education looks from home. It covers topics such as homework, school messages, and how welcome parents feel, and the answers shape what the school changes next term.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a parent survey?
faq_plan.a: Decide what the results should change, write about 10 questions on things parents see firsthand, translate them where families need it, and try the survey on two parents. Emergent's AI survey builder turns that plan, written as a plain description, into a working survey with a results view.

faq_plan.q: What are some good questions for a parent survey?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good questions for a parent survey?

prov.original: What are some good questions for a parent survey?

faq_plan.a: Good parent survey questions ask about things a parent sees and the school can change. Ask how easy it is to reach your child's teacher and how you prefer to hear school news. Ask whether you feel welcome at school events and whether the school helped you take part in decisions about your child. Close with one open question about what the school should do differently.

faq_plan.q: What should a parent survey template include?
faq_plan.a: A parent survey template needs a fixed core and a part that changes. Keep 8 to 10 core questions word for word every year, which lets this spring compare with last spring. Add a short section on this year's topic and one open question. Volunteer sign-ups belong in a separate volunteer survey. An Emergent-built survey keeps every year in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What are some parent survey examples?
faq_plan.a: Beyond the four on this page, schools run parent surveys on bus routes and start times, school lunch, and the move into kindergarten or middle school. A district may ask families to rank spending priorities before the budget is set. An Emergent-built survey has no response cap, even when a district sends it to every family on the same day.

Parent surveys give every family a say, including parents who miss evening meetings and never email a teacher. They also give a school a number to track. Texas tracks one for special education: its State Performance Plan Indicator 8 measures the percentage of parents with a child receiving special education services who report that schools facilitated parent involvement.

faq_plan.q: How often should a school run a parent survey?
faq_plan.a: Run one full parent survey a year, at the same point each year so the results compare, and add short check-ins of two or three questions after a single event, like a family night. Space them so a family never gets two surveys in the same month. At a parish school, the parish's church survey often reaches the same households. Agree on dates with the parish office first.

faq_plan.q: What rating scale works best on a parent survey?
faq_plan.a: A labeled five-point agreement scale works best for opinion questions. Keep the same scale on every rating question so the results line up, and add a 'does not apply' option for questions some families cannot answer, like those about the bus. For time and frequency, ask for a number, such as minutes of homework, instead of a rating.

faq_plan.q: How long should a parent survey stay open?
faq_plan.a: Keep a parent survey open for about 10 school days. State the closing date in the first message, send a final reminder two days before it closes, and schedule it away from testing weeks and holiday breaks. The app Emergent builds can send that reminder by email on the day you set. Leave a week after it closes to read the answers before anything is shared.

faq_plan.q: What should a parent survey ask after parent-teacher conferences?
faq_plan.a: It should ask two or three questions, sent the same evening: whether the time was long enough, whether you left knowing one next step for your child, and whether you want the next conference in person or by video. That short follow-up is a post event survey. Keep it apart from the yearly parent survey, where its answers would crowd the core questions.

plan.angle: Six of the top 10 are state agencies and districts hosting their own parent survey (Oklahoma, Arizona, Maryland, Philadelphia, Texas), so a searcher lands on someone else's survey link; one SurveyMonkey page lists questions. None shows how a school, a preschool or a PTO builds its own parent survey and what happens to the answers. This page shows four parent surveys running (the special education involvement survey the state pages host, a homework load check, a two-language preschool survey and a PTO spending vote), each with its numbers and the person who acts on them, then answers the question-list and template intent in the FAQ and the how-to.

openers.evidence: Full-sentence openers: 'Harlow Creek School District surveys each family...', 'Let each family pick a language on the first screen.', 'Name the decision the answers will feed...'.

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous detail ('wait in the pickup line', 'a laptop at conferences'); loose link analogies kept as a note.
